successors.name: Judea
successors.text: 'at the death of Zenodorus, Augustus gave Iturea to Herod the Great': the Iturean base and Zenodorus's Ulatha and Paneas

ledger.x: 105 BCE: the earliest date on the pages for the Iturean principality.
105 BCE: Aristobulus I attacks the Itureans.
103 BCE: the campaign ends with the Hasmonean royal title (judea dossier: 'Aristobulus I takes the royal title and conquers Galilee', 104-103).
103 BCE: Galilee passes to the Hasmoneans.
36 BCE: the dynasty of Ptolemy son of Mennaeus (85-40) and Lysanias ends with Lysanias's execution and Zenodorus holds on a lease.
36 BCE: Zenodorus holds Ulatha and Paneas on lease from Cleopatra.
20 BCE: Augustus gives Iturea to Herod the Great.
20 BCE: the Iturean principality ends with Zenodorus, who 'died soon afterwards in Antioch'; Herod the Great receives the land.

wars.name: Aristobulus I's campaign against Iturea
wars.outcome: 'In 105 BCE, Hasmonean leader Aristobulus I campaigned against Iturea'; the judea dossier has Galilee conquered by 103.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for the Iturean principality; the Beqaa and Mount Lebanon governorates, a circle on the Anti-Lebanon and (from 36) a circle at Ulatha and Paneas stand in.
